title: Consistency Is Not Validity: Self-Rewarded Moral Argumentation Makes Language Models Decisive but Pliable
abstract: arXiv:2610.30349v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLMs are increasingly consulted for moral judgment. We aim to improve performance on such tasks by rewarding good arguments, on the premise that arguing well increases the likelihood of judging well. We train a reinforcement learning policy initialized from a state-of-the-art language model in a self-judged tournament with masked thinking: the generated arguments are judged pairwise on argument quality by the policy itself. As an empirical basis, we extract authentic dilemmas from classic novels, using a logic solver to verify that each constitutes a conflict. We show that our judge rates argument quality like human annotators, and the policy then adopts the language register that it rewards. Testing on the external benchmarks MoralChoice, ELEPHANT, and MORABLES, we find that the policy becomes more decisive and invariant to the order in which options are presented, but sycophancy and reframing remain a challenge to validity. translated_title: 一致性并非有效性：自我奖励的道德论证使语言模型变得果断但易受影响
translated_abstract: 大语言模型越来越多地被用于道德判断咨询。我们旨在通过奖励好的论证来提升此类任务的性能，其前提是论证得当能够提高正确判断的可能性。我们从一个最先进的语言模型初始化一个强化学习策略，在一种掩蔽思维的自我评判锦标赛中进行训练：由策略本身对生成的论证就论证质量进行两两评判。作为实证基础，我们从经典小说中提取真实的道德困境，并使用逻辑求解器验证每个困境确实构成冲突。我们证明，我们的评判机制对论证质量的评分与人类标注者一致，策略随后会采用它所奖励的语言风格。在MoralChoice、ELEPHANT和MORABLES等外部基准上的测试表明，该策略变得更加果断，且对选项呈现顺序保持不变，但谄媚性和重新框架问题仍然是对有效性的挑战。
tldr: 该论文提出一种自我奖励的强化学习方法，让模型通过自我评判道德论证的质量来提升道德判断能力，使模型变得更加果断且不受选项呈现顺序的影响，但谄媚性和重新框架问题仍然存在。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes a self-rewarded reinforcement learning approach where the model judges the quality of its own moral arguments to improve moral judgment, making it more decisive and invariant to option ordering, though sycophancy and reframing remain challenges to validity.
